observation.visible_scene: A close-up of a CNC machining setup against a dark, softly lit background filled with a persistent hazy mist. An angled black spindle head with a metallic tool holder and a small slender end mill occupies the upper left, pointing down toward a shiny metal workpiece. The workpiece is a cylindrical block whose top has been machined into a set of curved, swept turbine/impeller blades, and it sits on a polished cylindrical base at the lower right.
visible_changes: Early in the clip the end mill tip is in contact with the left side of the bladed top, and over the first ~30 frames the tool traverses laterally along the upper edge of the blades from left toward right, staying engaged with the part.

From roughly the mid-clip onward the tool lifts and moves away from the workpiece; by the final frames there is a clear air gap between the cutter tip and the top of the blades, with the spindle assembly appearing higher and more to the left.
The workpiece's bladed structure and cylindrical base remain the same solid object throughout, with no visible deformation or material being removed within these frames.
The surrounding misty haze and the dark gradient background persist, with subtle shifts in haze brightness as the tool moves.

The framing of the whole scene drifts slightly (the workpiece shifts a little rightward in the frame while the spindle shifts leftward/upward), indicating possible camera movement in addition to the tool's own motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether this traversal is the beginning or end of a cutting pass, and what happens before/after the crop.
The actual material of the part, the tool's spin speed, and whether coolant spray (vs. mist) is active off-frame.
The machine's full geometry and any operator or control actions.
uncertain_details: It is hard to fully separate the tool's physical translation/retraction from a slow camera pan, since the background provides little fixed reference.
Exact points of tool–workpiece contact and whether any chips are produced are not clearly resolvable at this resolution.
The slight apparent size/position change of the spindle housing may be perspective/camera rather than pure tool motion.

and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
